correctness.rationale: Uniformity is explicit: choose L=loglog X, Y=L^(1/3), z=exp(L^2); Siegel-Walfisz for p<=Y and q>z plus Mertens for q<=z gives A_p=L/(p-1)+O(log L), B_p^2 likewise. Turan-Kubilius mean-square then bounds each two-witness failure by O(Xp/L). Sum p<=Y gives O(XL^(-1/3)); the local p-adic argument forces avoidance of p||n outside this union. CRT gives the exact finite product plus O(exp(2Y log Y)); Mertens on p=1 mod3 makes the product O_T((log L)^(-1/2)). Since L^(-1/3)=o((log L)^(-1/2)), the claim follows. Verified finite arithmetic checks were executed from the actual standalone verifier, but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: A first explicit convergence rate for all fixed thresholds of a natural divisor-sum GCD ratio is meaningful beyond the previously proved qualitative density limit. The rate uses growing-prime uniformity and is not a routine finite subfamily computation. It is slow but truly uniform in X with fixed T, naturally advances the quantitative arithmetic distribution problem, and does not overclaim optimality or numerical usefulness.
